chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-'Alawi, from al-'Umarki, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man in janabah, or not being in a state of wudu (ablution), who does not have water with him, while he comes upon snow and earth: which of the two is better? Should he perform tayammum, or wipe his face with snow? He said: Snow is better if he moistens his head and body with it; but if he is not able to perform ghusl with it, then let him perform tayammum.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: more preferable in legal application here
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state requiring ghusl due to janabah
key_terms.ثَلْجًا: snow used here as a possible means of purification
key_terms.صَعِيدًا: earth or clean ground used for tayammum
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the state of minor ritual purity
key_terms.يَتَمَسَّحُ: he wipes himself, here with snow
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum, the dry ablution
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلَ: he performs ghusl, the ritual washing of the body

ai.seo_question: If a person in janabah finds snow but no water, should he use the snow or perform tayammum?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about ritual purification when liquid water is unavailable but snow and earth are present. It states that using snow to wet the head and body is preferable when possible, and if that cannot be done, one should perform tayammum.
